title: Rosa Parks and Montgomery
subject: histoire
description: **December 1, 1955**, a seamstress refuses to give up her seat on a bus in Montgomery. His arrest launched a boycott of **381 days** and changed the civil rights movement.

hero.hook: One seat refused, 381 days of boycott, and the segregationist South begins to falter.

blocks.text: **December 1, 1955**, in Montgomery, capital of Alabama, a 42-year-old seamstress refuses to get up. Her name: **Rosa Parks**. A white passenger wants his seat. She says no.

It's not a whim. In the American South, the law still separates blacks and whites everywhere. His arrest sparked a bus boycott that lasted **381 days**. A young, still little-known pastor, **Martin Luther King Jr.**, found his voice there.

In the mid-1950s, the South lived under  laws. These rules impose racial separation: schools, hospitals, fountains, transport. In **1896**, a Supreme Court ruling, , even validated the idea “separate but equal”. [[Jim Crow laws]] [[Plessy v. Ferguson]]

On Montgomery buses, black people sit in the back. If the white area is full, those in the middle must stand up. Rosa Parks is not a random passenger. An activist for , an association for civil rights, she followed training at , a center where people learn non-violent resistance. His calm and respectability make him the ideal face for a public fight. [[The NAACP]] [[Highlander Folk School]]

That evening, driver James Blake orders four black passengers to stand up for one white person. Only Parks refuses. She is arrested. The next day, leaflets called for a boycott of buses on the day of his trial, December **5**.

Nine months earlier, **Claudette Colvin**, a 15-year-old high school student, had already refused to give up her seat. The activists had not put her forward: pregnant and single, she was considered too “fragile” to convince public opinion.

blocks.caption: The arrest of Rosa Parks, starting point of the boycott.

blocks.text: To hold on, the community created the Montgomery Improvement Association. At its head: Martin Luther King Jr., pastor of 26 years. On December 5, the buses ran almost empty. What was supposed to last a day becomes a standoff lasting more than a year.

Black people represent approximately **75%** of users. We organize carpooling. Taxis lower their prices to the price of the ticket. Repression follows: harassment, canceled insurance, threats. In January 1956, King's house was dynamited. Faced with the rubble, he calls for calm. This moment imposes its moral authority.

blocks.caption: During the boycott, Montgomery buses ran almost empty.

blocks.text: The bus company loses approximately **65%** of its revenue. Downtown businesses are suffering. What was a local conflict becomes a national affair: cameras across the country are watching Montgomery.

At the same time, the lawyers are relying on , the ruling which banned segregation in schools. **November 13, 1956**, Supreme Court Affirms: Alabama Bus Segregation Is Unconstitutional. On **December 21**, Parks and King symbolically board the front of a bus. [[Brown v. Board of Education (1954)]]

events.title: Arrest of Rosa Parks
events.detail: She refuses to give up her seat to Montgomery.

events.title: Start of the boycott
events.detail: The buses run empty; King takes the lead in the movement.

blocks.text: The price is heavy: Parks loses his job and leaves Montgomery under threats. But the model is launched. It will lead to , the major law which prohibits segregation in public places. [[Civil Rights Act of 1964]]
In **381 days**, the Montgomery boycott proves that organized civil disobedience can break down local segregation and reveal a leader: Martin Luther King.
